findings.summary: The budget was met by splitting five existing defaults so that the reader's first-sentence render drops their rules
findings.evidence: DefaultsModel::render uses first_sentence() (crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs:58-83). Before the change these five statements were one sentence each, so the reader saw all of each rule. After it, the reader sees only 'Adopt good, maintained tools and crates before building.', 'Every module has passing tests.', 'Everything committed is public: no secrets, credentials, or personal data.', 'Done means independently verified.' and 'Requests are short.'. The lost clauses include the core reader rule 'Recover hidden requirements from the repository before asking'. The CHANGELOG says this was done to fit the budget. Simpler, sound alternatives: write each new entry so its first sentence carries the whole rule, or shorten wording without adding sentence breaks, or raise the reader budget as the reading allowed in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs.

findings.summary: The reader's default context lacks the bump-command and silent-fallback halves of the new policies, so the reader can still ask those questions
findings.evidence: The rendered lines are 'Version pins in config, such as claude_version, stay exact and never float.' and 'A check never relies on inherited environment or ambient tools.'. The explicit runner tool paths, recording the tool used, 'silent fallback is a defect', the bump command and the 'Prose-only' marks never reach the reader. The request names 'silent runner fallback' as a question the reader keeps asking, and it asks for a test that shows the reading step's context includes these policies. The new test checks those phrases against the model instead, and its comment admits this.

findings.summary: The reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met
findings.evidence: The reading assumed the reader renders each default in full, so two new entries would cost about 100 tokens and the fix would be to trim root-cause and behavior-evidence. In fact render() shows only each statement's first sentence. So trimming the long later sentences saves nothing, and whatever a policy puts after its first sentence never reaches the reader. The reading should have required each new policy's first sentence to carry the whole rule the reader needs, including the bump command and the silent-fallback rule.

summary: Fail. Both entries are in defaults.toml with the requested wording, they parse, and fmt, clippy and tests pass. But the reader only ever sees the first sentence of each default, and the change works around that rule in two harmful ways. First, to fit the 2,000-token reader budget (now 1990), it split five existing one-sentence defaults so the reader no longer sees their second halves. Among the lost text is lazy-requests' rule to recover hidden requirements from the repository before asking. Second, the reader still does not see the bump-command rule or the silent-fallback rule, which are the questions the user wants it to stop asking. The new test checks those phrases in the full statements rather than in what the reader sees, and its own comment says so. A sound fix needs three things: each new default's first sentence carries its whole rule; the existing defaults stay as they were, or are shortened without adding sentence breaks; and if it still does not fit, the reader budget is raised, which the reading allowed as a fallback. Separately, docs/system-facts.md changed outside the listed deliverables; a test requires that change, so it is minor.
